P3400.title: Cylinder Deactivation System Bank 1
P3400.description: The engine control module has detected a fault in the cylinder deactivation system on bank 1. Variable displacement engines shut off cylinders under low load to save fuel — a fault here disables the function.

causes.label: Deactivation solenoid or oil control valve failed
Collapsing lifter stuck
Low oil pressure prevents activation

P3401.title: Cylinder 1 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Open
P3401.description: The engine control module has detected an open circuit at the cylinder 1 deactivation or intake valve control solenoid. Without a valid circuit, cylinder 1 cannot be deactivated.

causes.label: Solenoid coil open
Wiring or connector open
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P3402.title: Cylinder 1 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3402.description: This code reports that cylinder 1 does not respond as expected when the engine computer switches it off or back on, although the control circuit itself tests fine. Ford lists P3402 in its Variable Displacement Engine monitor for 2020-2023 gasoline engines: it runs continuously during deactivation, entry and exit, between 400 and 4500 rpm and once oil pressure has had about two seconds to build. GM handles the mechanical check for cylinder 1 under its own code P3498 instead. Wiring faults on the same channel set P3401, P3403 or P3404. A driver typically notices a warning lamp, a shake when the engine changes modes, or a misfire on cylinder 1.

causes.label: Low oil level, wrong viscosity or aged oil slows the hydraulic switching
Switchable lifter or rocker of cylinder 1 sticking or not latching
Deactivation solenoid valve sticking or its oil screen blocked
Leaking solenoid seal lets control pressure bleed off

symptoms: Shudder or jerk when the engine enters or leaves reduced-cylinder mode
Cylinder deactivation no longer used, higher fuel use

P3403.title: Cylinder 1 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3403.description: The engine computer drives the deactivation valve for cylinder 1 through an output stage that checks its own wiring. P3403 means that check found the control line pulled to ground. GM documents it for the L84 and L86 V8s (2019): with the driver off, an impedance below 0.5 ohm to ground counts as a fault, and 20 failures in 25 samples taken every 250 ms set a Type B code, so the lamp comes on after the second trip. Ford's VDE monitor flags the same short via its smart driver within 5 seconds. An open line is P3401, a short to battery voltage P3404, a mechanical failure P3402. The engine then stays in all-cylinder mode, mainly costing fuel.

causes.label: Control wire chafed against the engine and shorted to ground
Internal short in the cylinder 1 deactivation solenoid
Oil or water in the solenoid connector
Faulty output driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine lamp on after two trips
Engine no longer switches to reduced-cylinder mode

P3404.title: Cylinder 1 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3404.description: P3404 is the short-to-power counterpart within the cylinder 1 group. GM tests it while the low-side driver is switched on: if the output still shows less than 0.5 ohm to supply voltage, the current has no proper path through the solenoid, and 20 of 25 samples at 250 ms set a Type B fault. The test only runs with at least 11 V at the powertrain relay and about 425 rpm (L84; 400 rpm on the L86). Ford names P3404 for the single deactivating cylinder of its VDE engines. Typical culprits are a control wire touching a supply line or a solenoid with shorted windings. Compare P3403 (short to ground) and P3401 (open).

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage in the harness
Shorted winding in the cylinder 1 deactivation solenoid
Damaged output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Possible further circuit codes on other solenoids if a shared supply is affected

P3405.title: Cylinder 1 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3405.description: J2012 reserves P3405 for an open control circuit of a separate exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 1. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The common systems do not need it: in GM's Dynamic Fuel Management one solenoid per cylinder feeds oil to both intake and exhaust lifters, and Ford's VDE only lists intake codes for cylinder 1. A GM patent application uses one shared hydraulic valve and only sets the order, with the exhaust valves switched off and back on before the intake valves; a Ford patent watches the exhaust valve via exhaust pressure. A separate exhaust actuator would fall under CARB's output component rule, which asks for continuity checks. If used, an open coil or wire would set P3405, while P3401 covers the intake side and P3406-P3408 the other exhaust faults.

causes.label: Broken wire or loose terminal to the exhaust valve actuator
Open coil in the cylinder 1 exhaust valve actuator
Output driver fault in the engine control module

symptoms: Cylinder deactivation or valve switching disabled

P3406.title: Cylinder 1 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3406.description: Where an engine controls the exhaust valves of cylinder 1 separately, P3406 would mean the exhaust side does not follow the command although the circuit checks pass. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford holds a patent that detects an exhaust valve still opening after deactivation through pressure changes in the exhaust, and a GM patent, using one shared control valve, has the exhaust valves deactivate and also reactivate before the intake valves, so a lagging exhaust side is a real failure mode. Production systems from GM and Ford instead check the whole cylinder (GM P3498, Ford P3402). Electrical faults on this channel are P3405, P3407 and P3408; if the cylinder keeps pumping exhaust, the driver may feel roughness.

causes.label: Insufficient or degraded oil delays exhaust-side switching
Exhaust lifter or rocker of cylinder 1 not latching or unlatching
Exhaust valve actuator sticking

symptoms: Rough running or vibration in reduced-cylinder mode

P3407.title: Cylinder 1 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3407.description: P3407 stands for a short to ground in the control circuit of a dedicated exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 1. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, so there are no published thresholds. As an analogy, GM's intake-side code P3403 counts an impedance under 0.5 ohm to ground, seen with the driver off, as a fault. CARB requires such output circuits to be checked for shorts. Engines with one shared solenoid per cylinder, like GM's AFM and DFM V8s, report this fault under the intake-side codes instead. An open exhaust circuit would be P3405, a short to power P3408. The car usually keeps running normally on all cylinders, with a warning lamp.

causes.label: Actuator control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the exhaust valve actuator
Engine control module output stage fault

P3408.title: Cylinder 1 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3408.description: If an engine has its own actuator for the exhaust valves of cylinder 1, P3408 marks a control circuit that reads high, usually a short to battery voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. For comparison, GM checks the intake-side P3404 with the driver switched on and flags under 0.5 ohm to supply. A GM patent application switches intake and exhaust valves together through one shared hydraulic valve, exhaust side first, and describes no separate exhaust channel either. With one solenoid per cylinder, as on GM's DFM, the code is not needed. Siblings: P3405 open, P3406 function, P3407 short to ground; P3404 is the intake-side equivalent.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Shorted coil in the exhaust valve actuator
Output stage fault in the engine control module

P3409.title: Cylinder 2 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3409.description: P3409 is the open-circuit code for the deactivation control of cylinder 2. GM uses it on two very different engines. On the 3.6 L V6 (LGX, LGZ) cylinder 2 is one of the two active fuel management cylinders, and an engineering bulletin links P3409 to oil leaking from the rocker arm oil control valve in the camshaft cover. On the L84 V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management every cylinder has a solenoid; GM flags an open circuit when it sees more than 200 kohm with the driver off, 20 of 25 samples at 250 ms, Type B. Shorts are P3411 and P3412, a mechanical failure P3410. The driver sees a warning lamp and loses the fuel-saving mode.

causes.label: Oil leaking at the control valve and soaking its connector (GM 3.6 L V6)
Broken wire or loose pin in the cylinder 2 solenoid circuit
Open coil in the cylinder 2 deactivation solenoid
Engine control module output driver fault

symptoms: Oil residue around the valve cover control valve (V6)
No reduced-cylinder operation, higher fuel use

P340A.title: Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Bank 1
P340A.description: Generic electrical fault on the cylinder deactivation/intake valve control circuit on bank 1. The mechanism that switches off intake valves on selected cylinders cannot be commanded.

causes.label: Deactivation solenoid failed
Wiring break or unplugged connector

P340B.title: Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Bank 2
P340B.description: Generic electrical fault on the cylinder deactivation/intake valve control circuit on bank 2.

causes.label: Deactivation solenoid failed
Wiring break or unplugged connector

P340C.title: Deactivation/Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Bank 1
P340C.description: Generic electrical fault on the cylinder deactivation/exhaust valve control circuit on bank 1. On engines with cylinder deactivation the exhaust valves of a switched-off cylinder are held closed together with its intake valves, typically by switchable rocker arms or lifters that oil-pressure solenoids control; this code covers the bank's control circuit for the exhaust-side actuators. While it is faulty the module stops deactivating cylinders on that bank, so the engine runs on all cylinders and uses slightly more fuel.

causes.label: Deactivation solenoid failed
Wiring break or unplugged connector

symptoms: Cylinder deactivation inactive, slightly higher fuel consumption

P340D.title: Deactivation/Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Bank 2
P340D.description: Generic electrical fault on the cylinder deactivation/exhaust valve control circuit on bank 2. On engines with cylinder deactivation the exhaust valves of a switched-off cylinder are held closed together with its intake valves, typically by switchable rocker arms or lifters that oil-pressure solenoids control; this code covers the bank's control circuit for the exhaust-side actuators. While it is faulty the module stops deactivating cylinders on that bank, so the engine runs on all cylinders and uses slightly more fuel.

causes.label: Deactivation solenoid failed
Wiring break or unplugged connector

symptoms: Cylinder deactivation inactive, slightly higher fuel consumption

P3410.title: Cylinder 2 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3410.description: P3410 covers a cylinder 2 deactivation system that is electrically intact but does not do what is commanded, such as valves that keep opening or fail to return. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM checks this behavior on the L84 under its own code P3499, by watching manifold pressure while cylinder 2 should be off; Ford uses the matching cylinder 1 code P3402. GM bulletin 21-NA-036 for 3.6 L V6 engines shows how such faults appear in practice: oil leaking past the control valve or rockers that do not latch cause misfires on cylinder 2 (P0302). Circuit faults belong to P3409, P3411 and P3412. Expect roughness and lost economy.

causes.label: Oil bleeding past the control valve seal, pressure lost
Rocker or lifter of cylinder 2 not latching
Low or degraded oil
Broken solenoid tip left in the bore keeps a new valve from seating

symptoms: Misfire on cylinder 2, often after a reduced-cylinder phase

P3411.title: Cylinder 2 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3411.description: P3411 means the control output for the cylinder 2 deactivation valve sees a short to ground. GM lists it for the L84 V8 (2019), whose Dynamic Fuel Management can switch off any cylinder: below 0.5 ohm to ground with the low-side driver off, 20 failures in 25 samples every 250 ms, at least 11 V on the powertrain relay and 425 rpm. It is a Type B fault, so the lamp lights after two trips in a row. GM notes that some controllers set P3409 together with it. On engines where cylinder 2 cannot be deactivated the code has no use. The fix is usually in the wiring or the solenoid in the engine valley; P3412 is the short to power.

causes.label: Damaged insulation lets the control wire touch ground
Cylinder 2 solenoid shorted internally
Faulty engine control module driver

symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips
Dynamic Fuel Management inactive, engine stays on all cylinders

P3412.title: Cylinder 2 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3412.description: On GM's L84 V8 each cylinder, including cylinder 2, has a valve lifter oil solenoid bolted into the block valley. NHTSA's description of the system notes these solenoids are driven with peak-and-hold current for fast response. P3412 is set when the control line for cylinder 2 is shorted to supply voltage: GM checks it with the driver on and treats under 0.5 ohm to power as failed, 20 of 25 samples at 250 ms, Type B. In that state the computer cannot pull the solenoid properly and drops cylinder 2 from deactivation. Related codes are P3409 for an open circuit, P3411 for a short to ground and P3410 when the circuit is fine but the cylinder does not respond.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a voltage feed in the harness
Low-resistance coil in the cylinder 2 solenoid
Engine control module output stage fault

P3413.title: Cylinder 2 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3413.description: P3413 belongs to the exhaust half of the cylinder 2 block and reports an open control circuit for a separately driven exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The engines known to deactivate cylinder 2, GM's L84 V8 and the 3.6 L V6, switch intake and exhaust valves through one control valve per cylinder and therefore report circuit faults as P3409. The code would only apply to designs with their own control valve for the exhaust side; a GM patent application instead switches both sides with one shared valve and merely staggers them, exhaust first. CARB requires a continuity check for such output components. P3414 to P3416 complete the exhaust group. The driver would see a lamp and lose deactivation.

causes.label: Open wire or connector to the cylinder 2 exhaust actuator
Actuator coil open
Engine control module driver fault

P3414.title: Cylinder 2 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3414.description: P3414 would be set when the exhaust valves of cylinder 2 do not follow a deactivation or reactivation command on an engine with separate exhaust valve control. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The underlying problem is described in a Ford patent: an exhaust valve that still opens after deactivation shows up as pressure changes in the exhaust, and the controller can reactivate the cylinder or block further deactivation. GM's DFM engines report a cylinder whose intake and exhaust valves stay active under their own code P3499 instead. Electrical faults on this channel are P3413, P3415 and P3416, the intake-side function code is P3410.

causes.label: Exhaust-side lifter or rocker of cylinder 2 not switching
Low oil pressure or aerated oil
Exhaust actuator valve sticking

symptoms: Rough running when cylinders are switched off
Deactivation suspended by the engine computer

P3415.title: Cylinder 2 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3415.description: The engine control module has detected a low-side voltage fault (short to ground) on the cylinder 2 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid circuit. The system disables further cylinder deactivation requests until the circuit is repaired.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to ground
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3416.title: Cylinder 2 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3416.description: The engine control module has detected a high-side voltage fault (short to power) on the cylinder 2 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to power
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3417.title: Cylinder 3 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3417.description: The engine control module has detected an open or out-of-range circuit at the cylinder 3 deactivation or intake valve control solenoid. Cylinder 3 cannot be deactivated until the circuit is restored.

causes.label: Solenoid coil open
Wiring or connector open
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P3418.title: Cylinder 3 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3418.description: The engine control module has detected a performance fault on the cylinder 3 deactivation or intake valve control system — the response of the actuator does not match the commanded state.

causes.label: Lifter stuck collapsed
Engine oil pressure too low
Oil passage blocked or contaminated

P3419.title: Cylinder 3 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3419.description: The engine control module has detected a low-side voltage fault (short to ground) on the cylinder 3 deactivation or intake valve solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to ground
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P341A.title: Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Performance Bank 1
P341A.description: The intake valve deactivation system on bank 1 is electrically active but the mechanical response does not match commanded state. Often hydraulic pin sticking from sludge or low oil pressure.

causes.label: Oil sludge blocks deactivation pin
Low oil pressure

P341B.title: Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Performance Bank 2
P341B.description: The intake valve deactivation system on bank 2 is electrically active but the mechanical response does not match commanded state.

causes.label: Oil sludge blocks deactivation pin
Low oil pressure

P341C.title: Deactivation/Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Performance Bank 1
P341C.description: The exhaust valve deactivation system on bank 1 is electrically active but the mechanical response does not match commanded state.

causes.label: Oil sludge blocks deactivation pin

P341D.title: Deactivation/Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Performance Bank 2
P341D.description: The exhaust valve deactivation system on bank 2 is electrically active but the mechanical response does not match commanded state.

causes.label: Oil sludge blocks deactivation pin

P3420.title: Cylinder 3 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3420.description: The engine control module has detected a high-side voltage fault (short to power) on the cylinder 3 deactivation or intake valve solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to power
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3421.title: Cylinder 3 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3421.description: The engine control module has detected an open or out-of-range circuit at the cylinder 3 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid. Cylinder 3 cannot be deactivated on the exhaust side until the circuit is restored.

causes.label: Solenoid coil open
Wiring or connector open
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P3422.title: Cylinder 3 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3422.description: The engine control module has detected a performance fault on the cylinder 3 exhaust valve deactivation system — the actuator response does not match the commanded state.

causes.label: Lifter stuck collapsed
Engine oil pressure too low

P3423.title: Cylinder 3 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3423.description: The engine control module has detected a low-side voltage fault (short to ground) on the cylinder 3 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to ground
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3424.title: Cylinder 3 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3424.description: The engine control module has detected a high-side voltage fault (short to power) on the cylinder 3 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to power
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3425.title: Cylinder 4 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3425.description: Cylinder 4 is one of the four cylinders that classic V8 cylinder deactivation shuts off, together with 1, 6 and 7, both at GM (Active Fuel Management) and on the Chrysler 5.7 L Hemi with MDS. That makes P3425 one of the best documented codes in this range. GM's 2019 tables for the L84 and L86 flag an open when the off-state output shows more than 200 kohm, 20 of 25 samples, Type B. Chrysler lists it as Cylinder 4 Deactivation Control Circuit; a STAR case describes the driver-side exhaust manifold heat shield wearing through the solenoid harness and asks for at least 15 mm clearance. P3427 and P3428 cover shorts on the same circuit.

causes.label: Solenoid harness chafed through by the exhaust manifold heat shield (5.7 L Hemi)
Open coil in the cylinder 4 deactivation solenoid
Corroded or loose solenoid connector
Control module software needing an update (Chrysler TSB 18-002-25)

symptoms: Further circuit codes for cylinders 1, 6 and 7 if the shared harness is damaged

P3426.title: Cylinder 4 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3426.description: The engine control module has detected a performance fault on the cylinder 4 deactivation or intake valve control system — the actuator response does not match the commanded state.

causes.label: Lifter stuck collapsed
Engine oil pressure too low

P3427.title: Cylinder 4 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3427.description: The engine control module has detected a low-side voltage fault (short to ground) on the cylinder 4 deactivation or intake valve solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to ground
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3428.title: Cylinder 4 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3428.description: The engine control module has detected a high-side voltage fault (short to power) on the cylinder 4 deactivation or intake valve solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to power
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3429.title: Cylinder 4 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3429.description: The engine control module has detected an open or out-of-range circuit at the cylinder 4 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid. Cylinder 4 cannot be deactivated on the exhaust side until the circuit is restored.

causes.label: Solenoid coil open
Wiring or connector open
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P3430.title: Cylinder 4 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3430.description: The engine control module has detected a performance fault on the cylinder 4 exhaust valve deactivation system — the actuator response does not match the commanded state.

causes.label: Lifter stuck collapsed
Engine oil pressure too low

P3431.title: Cylinder 4 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3431.description: The engine control module has detected a low-side voltage fault (short to ground) on the cylinder 4 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to ground
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3432.title: Cylinder 4 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3432.description: The engine control module has detected a high-side voltage fault (short to power) on the cylinder 4 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid circuit. Cylinder deactivation is disabled while the fault is present.

causes.label: Wiring shorted to power
Solenoid internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P3433.title: Cylinder 5 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3433.description: P3433 reports an open control circuit to the deactivation valve of cylinder 5, and GM has used it across three generations. The 2007 V6 with Displacement on Demand, which shut off cylinders 1, 3 and 5, already flagged a short or open after 30 failures in 100 samples at 250 ms above 800 rpm. On the 3.6 L V6 (LGX, LGZ) cylinder 5 is an active fuel management cylinder, and GM tied P3433 to oil leaking from the rocker arm control valve in the camshaft cover. The 2019 L84 V8 tests every cylinder with a 200 kohm limit. Each time it is a Type B code. P3434 to P3436 are the function and short codes for the same cylinder.

causes.label: Oil leaking at the cylinder 5 control valve into its connector (GM 3.6 L V6)
Broken wire or spread terminal in the solenoid circuit
Open coil in the cylinder 5 solenoid
Engine control module output fault

symptoms: Oil seepage at the valve cover control valve (V6)

P3434.title: Cylinder 5 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3434.description: With P3434 the computer has found that cylinder 5 does not switch off or back on correctly, while the control circuit tests fine. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's L84 runs the equivalent test under P349C: manifold pressure stays too high while cylinder 5 is commanded off, meaning its valves keep working. For 3.6 L V6 engines, GM bulletin 21-NA-036 describes the field picture: misfires on cylinder 5 (P0305), sometimes only after a reduced-cylinder phase, from oil leaking past the control valve or rockers that do not latch, and asks to check for a solenoid tip broken off in the bore. Wiring faults for this cylinder are P3433, P3435 and P3436.

causes.label: Oil leaking past the cylinder 5 control valve seal
Switching rocker or lifter of cylinder 5 not latching
Solenoid tip broken off in the bore
Low or aged engine oil

P3435.title: Cylinder 5 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3435.description: P3435 flags a short to ground on the control line of the cylinder 5 deactivation valve. GM documents it codewise twice: in the 2019 tables for the L84 V8, with under 0.5 ohm to ground in the driver-off state, 20 of 25 samples at 250 ms and Type B, and in an engineering bulletin for 3.6 L V6 engines (LGX, LGZ) where P3435 appears along with P3433 and P3409 when oil leaks from the rocker arm control valve. Oil that wicks into the connector can create exactly such a leakage path. P3433 is the open circuit, P3436 the short to power, P3434 a mechanical failure. In daily driving the engine simply stays on all cylinders.

causes.label: Oil in the cylinder 5 valve connector creating a leakage path (GM 3.6 L V6)
Control wire shorted to ground
Shorted cylinder 5 solenoid
Engine control module driver fault

symptoms: Oil wetness at the valve cover around the control valve (V6)

P3436.title: Cylinder 5 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3436.description: P3436 is the short-to-power code for the cylinder 5 deactivation valve. Publicly it is documented by GM for the L84 V8 (2019), where Dynamic Fuel Management uses a dedicated valve lifter oil solenoid for each of the eight cylinders. The engine computer checks the line while its low-side driver is on; an impedance below 0.5 ohm toward supply voltage counts as a fault, confirmed by 20 of 25 samples at 250 ms, with at least 11 V and 425 rpm. As a Type B code it lights the lamp after two consecutive trips. Because the solenoid then cannot be switched in a controlled way, cylinder 5 is excluded from deactivation. Siblings: P3433 open, P3435 short to ground, P3434 function.

causes.label: Control wire touching a voltage supply
Shorted coil in the cylinder 5 solenoid
Engine control module output stage defect

symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips

P3437.title: Cylinder 5 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3437.description: P3437 is reserved for an open circuit in a separate exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 5. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, the main user of cylinder 5 deactivation codes (2007 V6, 3.6 L V6, L84 V8), only publishes the intake-side group P3433 to P3436, because its systems switch both valves of a cylinder together; NHTSA's description of Dynamic Fuel Management states that each solenoid feeds intake and exhaust lifters. CARB still expects any emission-relevant actuator to be checked for continuity, which is what this code would report. P3438 to P3440 are the other exhaust codes for cylinder 5, P3433 the intake-side open.

causes.label: Broken wire or connector to the cylinder 5 exhaust actuator
Open actuator coil
Engine control module driver fault

P3438.title: Cylinder 5 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3438.description: P3438 describes an exhaust side of cylinder 5 that is commanded to deactivate or reactivate but does not follow, with an intact circuit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Two patents show why the exhaust side matters: in a GM patent application one shared valve switches the exhaust valves off, and back on, before the intake valves, so an exhaust lifter that lags breaks that order, and Ford detects an exhaust valve still opening after deactivation from exhaust pressure. If the exhaust valve keeps opening while the cylinder is off, the engine can run rough. GM's DFM engines report a cylinder whose valves stay active as P349C. The electrical codes for this channel are P3437, P3439 and P3440.

causes.label: Exhaust lifter or rocker of cylinder 5 slow to switch
Insufficient oil pressure for switching
Exhaust actuator valve sticking

symptoms: Roughness or noise while cylinders are switched off

P3439.title: Cylinder 5 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3439.description: P3439 would report a short to ground in the control circuit of a dedicated exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 5. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no threshold is published for it. The closest documented reference is the intake-side P3435, which GM's L84 sets at under 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver off, after 20 of 25 samples. CARB's output component rules call for exactly this kind of short-circuit check on any actuator that can affect emissions. Engines that switch both valves of cylinder 5 with one solenoid report a short only through P3435. Exhaust-side siblings are P3437 (open), P3438 (function) and P3440 (short to power).

causes.label: Control wire of the exhaust actuator grounded
Internally shorted exhaust actuator
Faulty engine control module output

symptoms: Engine runs on all cylinders only

P3440.title: Cylinder 5 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3440.description: P3440 closes the cylinder 5 block and stands for a high signal, usually a short to supply voltage, in the circuit of a separate exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The code only makes sense on an engine with a separate exhaust actuator; a Ford patent, for example, checks via exhaust pressure whether an exhaust valve still opens after deactivation. Current production systems that deactivate cylinder 5 drive both valves from one solenoid, and GM reports a short to power there as P3436, checked with the driver on and a 0.5 ohm limit. If a dedicated exhaust channel did short high, the computer would stop using deactivation and light the lamp. Compare P3437, P3438 and P3439.

causes.label: Exhaust actuator control wire shorted to voltage
Shorted actuator coil
Engine control module output stage fault

P3441.title: Cylinder 6 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3441.description: Cylinder 6 belongs to both classic V8 deactivation groups, so P3441 is a code that real engines set. On GM V8s with Active Fuel Management, which park cylinders 1, 7, 6 and 4, the 2019 tables list it for the L86 truck engine and the LT4 Corvette: with the low-side driver off, more than 200 kohm between output and ground counts as an open, and 20 failures in 25 samples (every 250 ms, from 400 rpm) store a Type B code. The L84 with Dynamic Fuel Management runs the same check from 425 rpm. Chrysler names P3441 for the 5.7 L Hemi with MDS; a STAR case blames a heat shield rubbing through the solenoid harness. Shorts on this circuit are P3443 and P3444.

causes.label: Solenoid harness broken or chafed through (on the 5.7 L Hemi by the manifold heat shield)
Open coil in the cylinder 6 deactivation solenoid
Loose or corroded connector at the cylinder 6 solenoid
Control module software that needs an update (Chrysler TSB 18-002-25)

symptoms: Engine no longer drops to four-cylinder mode
Possibly circuit codes for cylinders 1, 4 and 7 as well if the shared harness is damaged

P3442.title: Cylinder 6 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3442.description: P3442 would flag cylinder 6 failing to switch off or back on while its control circuit is electrically sound. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Both large users of cylinder 6 deactivation picked their own numbers instead: GM's L84 reports a cylinder 6 that keeps breathing as P349D, judged from filtered manifold pressure in 22 of 25 opportunities (Type B), and Chrysler's 5.7 L Hemi uses P1416, Cylinder 6 Reactivation Control Performance. GM also warns that P349D can set after a voltage dip during cranking, which an ECM update cures. Real mechanical faults usually trace back to the oil supply or a lifter that does not latch. Electrical faults on the same channel are P3441, P3443 and P3444.

causes.label: Oil level too low, wrong grade or worn oil, so pressure builds too slowly
Deactivating lifter of cylinder 6 not locking or unlocking
Cylinder 6 solenoid valve sticking or its oil screen clogged
Code stored after a voltage dip during cranking, cured by an ECM update (GM analogue 20-NA-204)

symptoms: Jerk or vibration when the engine changes between eight and four cylinders
Fuel consumption rises because deactivation is locked out

P3443.title: Cylinder 6 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3443.description: Here the engine computer has found the cylinder 6 solenoid's switched lead pulled to ground. GM spells out the test for its 2019 V8s (L84, L86 and the LT4 Corvette): while the low-side driver is off, an impedance under 0.5 ohm toward ground is a fault, and 20 hits among 25 checks while the powertrain relay supplies at least 11 V store a Type B code. GM adds that some controllers record the open-circuit code P3441 at the same moment, so the pair does not prove two separate faults. On the L84 each solenoid also has a high-side feed, and a short to ground there carries GM's own code P3114. P3444 is the short to voltage on this channel. Cylinder deactivation stays off until the fault is repaired.

causes.label: Insulation of the cylinder 6 control wire worn through to ground
Cylinder 6 solenoid shorted internally to its housing
Moisture or oil bridging the pins of the solenoid connector
Output stage in the engine control module damaged

symptoms: Check engine lamp on from the second faulty trip
P3441 stored at the same time on some GM controllers

P3444.title: Cylinder 6 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3444.description: P3444 is set when the output that switches the cylinder 6 deactivation solenoid to ground still sees supply voltage while it is turned on, meaning the line has a short to power instead of a path through the coil. GM tests this on the 2019 L84, L86 and LT4 V8s with a limit of 0.5 ohm to controller power, 20 errors out of 25 samples at 250 ms intervals and Type B lamp logic. On the L84, whose solenoids also have a switched high-side feed, a short to voltage on that feed has the separate GM code P3115. Because the ECM can no longer energize the valve, cylinder 6 simply keeps firing and the engine gives up four-cylinder operation. Compare P3441 (open) and P3443 (short to ground).

causes.label: Cylinder 6 control wire in contact with a supply wire in the harness
Shorted turns in the cylinder 6 solenoid coil
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Engine runs on all eight cylinders permanently
Slightly higher fuel consumption at light load

P3445.title: Cylinder 6 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3445.description: P3445 is defined for a break in the wiring of a stand-alone actuator that would control the exhaust valves of cylinder 6. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The engines that deactivate cylinder 6 today, GM's AFM and DFM V8s and Chrysler's Hemi with MDS, publish only intake-side codes for this cylinder (P3441, and at GM also P3443 and P3444). NHTSA's description of GM's DFM hardware explains why: a single solenoid per cylinder sends oil to the intake and the exhaust lifters alike, which then unlock one after the other. An engine with its own exhaust-side actuators would have to check their wiring for continuity under CARB's rules for output components, and that is the fault this code names. P3446 to P3448 complete the exhaust group.

causes.label: Broken wire or loose connector at the cylinder 6 exhaust actuator
Actuator coil interrupted
Output stage in the control module faulty

P3446.title: Cylinder 6 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3446.description: P3446 stands for an exhaust valve on cylinder 6 that does not follow a deactivation or reactivation command although its circuit is intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM watches a closely related failure under a code of its own: on the 2019 L84, P318E (Cylinder 6 Trapped High Pressure Exhaust Charge) looks for an exhaust valve that fails to open and let the burned gas out, recognised by crankshaft jerk in 66 of 100 samples, Type B, with immediate protective action. A Ford patent covers the opposite case, an exhaust valve that keeps opening after shut-off, detected from exhaust pressure. The electrical codes for this exhaust channel are P3445, P3447 and P3448.

causes.label: Exhaust lifter of cylinder 6 switching late or not at all
Oil pressure too low for reliable switching
Exhaust control valve sticking

symptoms: Knock-like noise or vibration when the cylinder is switched back on

P3447.title: Cylinder 6 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3447.description: P3447 is about a ground fault on the lead of a stand-alone exhaust actuator for cylinder 6. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, the one maker publishing the full set of cylinder 6 circuit codes, switches both valves of the cylinder with one solenoid and reports a ground short as the intake-side P3443: impedance below 0.5 ohm toward ground while the driver is off, 20 of 25 samples, Type B. A comparable test would apply here, because CARB requires circuit monitoring for every emission-relevant output. NHTSA notes that GM inhibits deactivation as soon as a solenoid driver circuit fault is present, so the practical result is an engine running on all cylinders. P3445 (open) and P3448 (short to power) are the neighbouring exhaust codes.

causes.label: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 6 chafed against the engine
Internal short to ground in the exhaust actuator
Damaged driver in the engine control module

P3448.title: Cylinder 6 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3448.description: If cylinder 6 had its own exhaust valve actuator, P3448 would report its control line shorted to battery voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A GM patent application on cylinder deactivation switches both sides through one shared hydraulic valve and only lets the exhaust valves go first, off and back on, so it shows no separate exhaust control either; GM's production V8s likewise put both lifters on one solenoid and publish only P3444 for a short to power on cylinder 6. That test, below 0.5 ohm to power with the driver switched on and 20 of 25 samples, is the reference for how such a fault would be judged. With the actuator unusable, deactivation is blocked. P3445 to P3447 are the sibling exhaust codes.

causes.label: Exhaust actuator wire touching a supply line
Shorted turns in the exhaust actuator coil of cylinder 6
Engine control module output stage faulty

P3449.title: Cylinder 7 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3449.description: P3449 tells you the engine computer lost continuity in the circuit to the cylinder 7 deactivation solenoid. Chrysler documents it twice for the 5.7 L Hemi with MDS: a 2025 bulletin for the 2023 RAM 1500 eTorque lists it next to a cylinder 7 misfire (P0307) and fixes it with new PCM software, and a STAR case names P3449 first when the driver-side manifold heat shield has worn through the MDS harness at the rear of the cylinder head. GM uses the code on AFM V8s (L86, LT4 Corvette) and on the DFM L84, flagging more than 200 kohm in the off state, 20 of 25 samples, Type B. P3451 and P3452 report shorts, P3450 a mechanical fault on cylinder 7.

causes.label: MDS harness at the rear of the driver-side head worn through by the manifold heat shield (5.7 L Hemi)
Cylinder 7 solenoid coil open
Solenoid connector loose or corroded
PCM calibration needing an update (Chrysler TSB 18-002-25)

symptoms: Rough idle or misfire on cylinder 7 (P0307) on the 5.7 L Hemi

P3450.title: Cylinder 7 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3450.description: P3450 is meant for a cylinder 7 whose valves do not switch as commanded while the solenoid circuit itself checks out. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In practice the lifters do the switching: NHTSA's account of GM's system shows oil pressure pushing spring-loaded locking pins inward so the lifter body moves without lifting the valve, and DFM only engages with coolant between 40 and 126 °C, more than 20 s of running and above 13 km/h. When that mechanism fails on cylinder 7, GM's L84 sets P349E from manifold pressure, and Chrysler's Hemi sets P1417, Cylinder 7 Reactivation Control Performance. P3449, P3451 and P3452 are the electrical codes for the same cylinder.

causes.label: Locking pins in a cylinder 7 lifter sticking from wear or dirt
Insufficient or aged oil delaying the switch
Oil screen or passage to the cylinder 7 solenoid blocked
Leaking O-ring on the solenoid lets pressure escape

symptoms: Ticking noise from the valve train

P3451.title: Cylinder 7 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3451.description: P3451 means the switched ground line of the cylinder 7 deactivation solenoid has contact with ground somewhere along its way. GM documents the check for the L84 and L86 trucks and the LT4 Corvette (2019): with the driver off, less than 0.5 ohm to ground, 20 hits in 25 samples taken every 250 ms, Type B, meaning the warning lamp waits for a second faulty trip. According to GM, certain controllers log the open-circuit code P3449 along with it, so both codes together need not mean two faults. On the L84 the high-side feed of the same solenoid reports a ground short under its own code P3117. P3452 is the short to power on this channel, P3450 the mechanical fault.

causes.label: Cylinder 7 control wire pinched or chafed to ground
Cylinder 7 solenoid shorted internally
Oil or water inside the solenoid connector
Defective driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine lamp on after two trips
P3449 may be stored as well
No four-cylinder mode, higher fuel use

P3452.title: Cylinder 7 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3452.description: Unlike the open and ground-short checks, GM can only detect P3452 while the cylinder 7 solenoid driver is switched on, because a short to supply voltage shows up as an output that will not pull low when it should. The 2019 tables for the L84, L86 and LT4 set the limit at 0.5 ohm to controller power and need 20 errors out of 25 samples, Type B. The check therefore depends on the ECM actually commanding deactivation; on GM's DFM engines that only happens with coolant above 40 °C, more than 20 s after start and above 13 km/h, according to NHTSA. Typical causes are a harness pressed against a feed wire or a solenoid with shorted windings. P3449 and P3451 are the other circuit codes for cylinder 7.

causes.label: Cylinder 7 control wire shorted to a voltage feed
Low-resistance coil in the cylinder 7 solenoid
Engine control module driver defective

symptoms: Check engine lamp on, often only after longer warm drives

P3453.title: Cylinder 7 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3453.description: P3453 is the code SAE assigns to an open circuit in a dedicated exhaust valve actuator for cylinder 7. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's description of Dynamic Fuel Management, published by NHTSA, shows how exhaust control works without such an actuator: the same oil signal unlocks the intake lifter at once, while the exhaust lifter waits until the valve spring load drops on the base circle of the cam. Separate wiring exists only in designs with an extra exhaust actuator, and CARB would require its continuity to be monitored. Actual cylinder 7 circuit faults on GM and Chrysler V8s show up as P3449 instead. P3454 to P3456 are the other exhaust codes; P3455 is the short to ground.

causes.label: Interrupted wire to the cylinder 7 exhaust actuator
Burnt-out actuator coil
Corroded actuator connector

P3454.title: Cylinder 7 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3454.description: P3454 covers an exhaust valve on cylinder 7 that does not switch as commanded, with no electrical fault on its control circuit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's own cylinder 7 check P318F on the 2019 L84 shows why the exhaust side matters: if the exhaust valve fails to open and release the burned gas, the trapped charge is compressed again, cylinder pressure climbs and the intake mechanism can be damaged on reactivation, so the ECM reacts at once (crankshaft jerk test, 66 of 100 samples, Type B). A Ford patent tackles the reverse problem, an exhaust valve still opening after deactivation, spotted through exhaust pressure. P3453, P3455 and P3456 are the electrical codes.

causes.label: Exhaust lifter of cylinder 7 stuck in the unlocked state
Oil pressure or oil quality inadequate for switching
Exhaust control valve slow or sticking

symptoms: Hard knock or jolt when cylinder 7 is reactivated

P3455.title: Cylinder 7 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3455.description: The engine control module has detected a low voltage condition in the control circuit of the cylinder 7 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid. A short to ground or low-side driver fault prevents proper actuation of the exhaust valve during cylinder deactivation events on cylinder 7.

causes.label: Solenoid or wiring shorted to ground
ECM low-side driver failed
Connector corrosion or pin damage

P3456.title: Cylinder 7 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3456.description: P3456 would flag a cylinder 7 exhaust valve actuator whose control line is shorted to supply voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. According to NHTSA's summary of the DFM system, GM drives its deactivation solenoids with peak-and-hold current drivers for fast, repeatable switching, and one solenoid serves both valves of the cylinder, so a short to power is caught under the intake-side code P3452 instead (below 0.5 ohm to power with the driver on, 20 of 25 samples, Type B). CARB requires such a check for any emission-relevant output, which is why the exhaust code exists at all. A short to ground on the same channel is P3455, an open circuit P3453, a mechanical fault P3454.

causes.label: Actuator wire of cylinder 7 shorted to battery voltage
Exhaust actuator coil with shorted turns
Current driver in the control module failed

symptoms: Engine does not enter reduced-cylinder mode

P3457.title: Cylinder 8 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3457.description: Cylinder 8 is not among the cylinders that classic Active Fuel Management or Chrysler's MDS shut off (both use 1, 4, 6 and 7), so P3457 is documented only for newer designs. GM's 2019 tables list it for the L84 with Dynamic Fuel Management, which can deactivate every cylinder: more than 200 kohm with the low-side driver off, 20 of 25 samples every 250 ms from 425 rpm, Type B. GM's AFM/DFM information bulletin adds that the LTA and LT2 engines deactivate cylinders 2, 3, 5 and 8. GM also notes that some controllers store P3459 together with an open. P3458 is the function code for cylinder 8, P3459 and P3460 the short-circuit codes.

causes.label: Wire to the cylinder 8 solenoid broken or chafed in the lifter valley harness
Open winding in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Poor contact at the solenoid connector
Engine control module output stage faulty

symptoms: P3459 may be stored alongside on some GM controllers

P3458.title: Cylinder 8 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3458.description: P3458 describes a cylinder 8 that does not deactivate or reactivate as commanded although its control circuit is electrically fine. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, the only maker with published cylinder 8 deactivation codes, files this failure under P349F on the L84: during a commanded skip, filtered manifold pressure stays above a threshold, which means the intake and exhaust valves kept working; the test runs with air charge above 120 mg and MAP/BARO between 0.30 and 0.95, and 22 failures in 25 opportunities give a Type B code. Bulletin 20-NA-204 adds that on 2021 full-size SUVs with L84 and L87 a voltage dip during cranking can set P349F without any hardware fault. Electrical faults are P3457, P3459 and P3460.

causes.label: Cylinder 8 deactivation lifter not unlocking or relocking
Oil pressure too low or oil aerated
Cylinder 8 solenoid valve sluggish or its screen blocked
False entry after low voltage while cranking, fixed by ECM update (GM analogue 20-NA-204)

symptoms: Check engine lamp on, sometimes going out again
Shake or roughness in light-load cruising

P3459.title: Cylinder 8 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3459.description: When the ground-side control line of the cylinder 8 deactivation solenoid touches ground, the ECM stores P3459. GM publishes this test for the 2019 L84 V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management: driver off, impedance below 0.5 ohm to ground, a minimum of 11 V on the relay feed and 425 rpm, 20 errors in 25 samples, Type B. Some GM controllers log P3457 at the same time. Because a DFM engine may skip any cylinder, a fault on cylinder 8 shuts down a system that otherwise uses this cylinder routinely; GM's LTA and LT2 also include cylinder 8 in their fixed deactivation set. A ground short on the solenoid's high-side feed has its own GM code, P311A. P3460 is the short to power.

causes.label: Cylinder 8 control wire grounded through damaged insulation
Internal short in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Contamination in the solenoid connector
Output driver in the engine control module damaged

symptoms: Check engine lamp on after the second trip
Engine runs on all eight cylinders at all times

P3460.title: Cylinder 8 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3460.description: P3460 reports a short to supply voltage on the control circuit of the cylinder 8 deactivation solenoid, found while the output is switched on. GM lists it for the 2019 L84: under 0.5 ohm between output and controller power, 20 of 25 samples spaced 250 ms apart, Type B, with the same 11 V and 425 rpm enable limits as the other cylinder 8 circuit checks. GM's table contains a slip here: the strategy column for P3460 speaks of the cylinder 7 solenoid, while code and component name cylinder 8. Typical causes are harness damage against a feed wire or a solenoid with shorted turns; the visible result is that the engine stops using cylinder 8 deactivation. Siblings: P3457 (open) and P3459 (short to ground).

causes.label: Cylinder 8 control wire in contact with a voltage source
Shorted turns in the cylinder 8 solenoid
Faulty driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Cylinder deactivation inactive, slightly higher fuel use

P3461.title: Cylinder 8 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3461.description: In the J2012 scheme, P3461 marks lost continuity to an exhaust-side actuator of its own on cylinder 8. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In the published sources, cylinder 8 is deactivated only by GM's newer V8s (DFM on the L84 and L87, a fixed 2-3-5-8 pattern on the LTA and LT2), and per NHTSA those engines feed both lifters of a cylinder from one solenoid, leaving no separate exhaust wiring to test. A GM patent application likewise uses one shared hydraulic valve and only staggers the exhaust valves ahead of the intake valves; only a separate exhaust actuator would fall under CARB's continuity check for output components. P3462 to P3464 are the other cylinder 8 exhaust codes, P3457 the intake-side open.

causes.label: Wire or plug to the cylinder 8 exhaust actuator broken
Exhaust actuator winding open
Control module output defective

P3462.title: Cylinder 8 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3462.description: With P3462 the ECM would be saying that the exhaust valve of cylinder 8 ignores deactivation commands even though nothing is wrong electrically. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM covers the exhaust side of cylinder 8 on the 2019 L84 with its own code P3190, Cylinder 8 Trapped High Pressure Exhaust Charge: if crankshaft jerk, normalized by engine speed, exceeds a load-dependent threshold while the cylinder is deactivated, the exhaust valve is judged not to have opened, and 66 failures in 100 samples set a Type B code. Ford patented the complementary check for an exhaust valve that keeps opening after deactivation, based on exhaust pressure. Symptoms range from vibration in reduced-cylinder mode to a misfire on cylinder 8 (P0308).

causes.label: Exhaust lifter of cylinder 8 failing to relock in time
Oil supply to the lifter gallery insufficient
Exhaust-side control valve sticking

P3463.title: Cylinder 8 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3463.description: P3463 would mean that the control line of a dedicated cylinder 8 exhaust actuator is shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. On the only engines with documented cylinder 8 deactivation, GM's L84 and its relatives, one solenoid handles both valves, and GM reports a ground short on it as P3459, testing for less than 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver off. NHTSA's summary of the system lists solenoid driver circuit faults among the reasons the ECM inhibits deactivation, which is also what a driver would notice here: the engine keeps all eight cylinders running and uses a little more fuel. P3461 covers an open, P3462 the function and P3464 a short to power in this exhaust group.

causes.label: Cylinder 8 exhaust actuator wire shorted to the engine block
Exhaust actuator shorted to ground internally
Driver stage in the engine control module faulty

symptoms: Engine stays on all eight cylinders

P3464.title: Cylinder 8 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3464.description: The engine control module has detected a high voltage condition in the control circuit of the cylinder 8 exhaust valve deactivation solenoid. A short to voltage or open low-side path causes the driver to read above the expected range, disabling cylinder deactivation requests for cylinder 8.

causes.label: Solenoid or wiring shorted to power
Solenoid coil open
ECM driver failed

P3465.title: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3465.description: P3465 flags an open circuit to the actuator meant to shut down cylinder 9 or hold its intake valve closed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Among such engines, Mercedes' M137 V12 (S 600 and CL 600, 1998 to 2002) had a shut-off system built around a solenoid pack and oil pressure tubes, whereas Audi's R8 V10 idles a whole bank by stopping injection and ignition. For orientation, GM treats the comparable circuit on its V8s as open above 200 kohm with the driver off, 20 failures in 25 samples. P3467 and P3468 cover shorts on the same line, P3466 a mechanical fault, P3469 the exhaust side of cylinder 9.

causes.label: Broken or chafed wire to the cylinder 9 actuator
Open coil in the cylinder 9 solenoid
Loose or corroded connector at the solenoid pack
Output stage in the engine control module failed

symptoms: Slightly higher fuel consumption at part load

P3466.title: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3466.description: P3466 is the plausibility test for cylinder 9: its actuator circuit is electrically sound, yet the cylinder fails to change state when the engine computer commands it. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. In valve-based systems the switching happens hydraulically; NHTSA's account of GM's design describes oil pressure moving locking pins inside the lifter. The Mercedes M137 V12, whose shut-off system relied on a solenoid pack and oil pressure tubes, is known for trouble with exactly those parts, exactly the kind of fault this code targets. Bank-switching V10 and W12 engines from Audi and Bentley leave the valves running and have nothing comparable to check. P3465, P3467 and P3468 are the electrical faults of cylinder 9.

causes.label: Oil level, pressure or quality too poor to switch cylinder 9
Leak at the oil tubes or solenoid pack feeding cylinder 9
Switching lifter of cylinder 9 sticking
Solenoid valve slow or sticking mechanically

symptoms: Rough running while switching between full and partial mode

P3467.title: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3467.description: With P3467 the control line of the cylinder 9 deactivation or intake valve actuator reads too low, which usually means it is touching ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Twelve-cylinder engines with cylinder shut-off do exist, for instance Mercedes' M137 and Lamborghini's Aventador V12 introduced in 2012, but no published diagnostic list connects this number to them. GM's matching test on its V8 engines looks for less than 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver switched off and only runs above 11 V and 425 rpm. On a low-side driven solenoid, a ground fault can keep the coil energised, so the cylinder may drop out when it should fire. Siblings: P3465 open circuit, P3468 short to voltage.

causes.label: Cylinder 9 control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the cylinder 9 solenoid
Moisture in the solenoid connector
Faulty driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Possible misfire on cylinder 9 if the actuator stays energised

P3468.title: Cylinder 9 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3468.description: P3468 indicates that the control circuit for the cylinder 9 deactivation or intake valve actuator is pulled high, typically by a short to battery voltage that the module notices once it switches the output on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Most engines above eight cylinders that shut cylinders down, such as Audi's R8 V10 and Bentley's W12, do so bank by bank without dedicated valve actuators; Mercedes' M137 V12, by contrast, used a solenoid pack. GM's eight-cylinder version of this check counts below 0.5 ohm to controller power with the driver on, 20 of 25 samples. Expect the module to shut the output off and run all cylinders. P3465 (open) and P3467 (ground short) are the other electrical faults here.

causes.label: Cylinder 9 control wire touching a supply wire
Shorted turns in the cylinder 9 solenoid coil
Output stage of the engine control module damaged

symptoms: Engine runs on all cylinders at all times

P3469.title: Cylinder 9 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3469.description: P3469 is set when the circuit driving a separate exhaust valve actuator on cylinder 9 is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. A distinct exhaust actuator only exists where intake and exhaust valves are switched independently; a GM patent at least shows that the exhaust valves can follow their own timing, being deactivated before the intake valves and reactivated before them too. GM's own production system uses one solenoid per cylinder for both valves, and the publicly described ten- and twelve-cylinder systems (Audi R8 V10, Bentley W12) keep the valves moving altogether. So an open circuit here can only concern an engine that carries such hardware. P3471 and P3472 report shorts, P3470 a functional fault, P3465 the intake side.

causes.label: Open or chafed wire to the cylinder 9 exhaust actuator
Exhaust actuator coil of cylinder 9 open
Connector at the exhaust actuator loose or corroded
Engine control module output failed

P3470.title: Cylinder 9 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3470.description: P3470 covers a cylinder 9 exhaust valve that does not follow its deactivation command although the control circuit shows no electrical fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The risk behind it is described in a Ford patent: an exhaust valve that keeps opening after shut-off spoils the gas cushion in the cylinder and can be detected from changes in exhaust pressure. The opposite case, a valve that stays shut on reactivation, traps hot gas under pressure. Neither the Lamborghini Aventador V12 nor the Huracán V10 publishes how their bank shut-off works, and Audi's V10 simply cuts injection and ignition, so this check has no known user. Electrical faults of the same actuator: P3469, P3471, P3472.

causes.label: Exhaust switching element of cylinder 9 stuck
Insufficient oil pressure for the exhaust switch
Exhaust actuator sluggish

symptoms: Knock or jolt when cylinder 9 comes back in

P3471.title: Cylinder 9 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3471.description: A low reading on the control line of the cylinder 9 exhaust valve actuator triggers P3471, most often a wire grounded against the engine or body. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Because known shut-off systems on engines above eight cylinders either drop a whole bank by fuel and spark (Audi R8 V10) or close the valves with one shared actuator per cylinder (as in GM's design), a separately wired exhaust actuator on cylinder 9 would be unusual. If such a circuit is present, test it the same way as the intake circuit: resistance to ground with the connector unplugged, then the coil. P3469 is the open-circuit fault, P3472 the short to voltage, P3467 the matching intake code.

causes.label: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 9 grounded
Internal short in the exhaust actuator
Engine control module output damaged

P3472.title: Cylinder 9 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3472.description: P3472 records a high voltage level on the cylinder 9 exhaust valve control circuit, the pattern of a wire shorted to a supply feed or of a coil with shorted windings. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Engines that could in principle have a cylinder 9 with deactivation include the Mercedes M137 V12, the Lamborghini Aventador V12 and Bentley's W12; for none of them is a separate exhaust actuator documented, and the Bentley engine is described as leaving its valves working during shut-off. A US patent from GM shows that the exhaust side has a sequence of its own: there the exhaust valves stop before the intake valves and also return first. P3469 (open) and P3471 (low) complete the electrical set.

causes.label: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 9 shorted to voltage
Shorted windings in the exhaust actuator
Faulty engine control module output

symptoms: Cylinder deactivation switched off by the control module

P3473.title: Cylinder 10 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3473.description: P3473 reports an open circuit to the deactivation or intake valve actuator of cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The V10 engines known for cylinder shut-off are Audi's 5.2 FSI in the R8 and Lamborghini's Huracán from model year 2016. Audi says its system idles one bank in the upper four gears by switching off injection and ignition, so it needs no valve actuator that this code could watch. On a twelve-cylinder engine with valve deactivation the code would mean a broken wire, an open coil or a bad connector at cylinder 10. P3475 and P3476 deal with shorts, P3474 with the mechanical result, P3477 with the exhaust valve.

causes.label: Wire to the cylinder 10 actuator open or chafed
Cylinder 10 solenoid coil open
Corroded or loose connector at cylinder 10
Engine control module driver failed

symptoms: Engine no longer switches to reduced-cylinder mode

P3474.title: Cylinder 10 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3474.description: P3474 is about function rather than wiring: cylinder 10 should shut down or come back, but measured engine behaviour says it did not, while its control circuit is intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Audi's R8 V10, one of the few ten-cylinder engines with shut-off, works without valve switching; Audi reserves the valve-closing method with zero-lift cams on axially sliding sleeves for its 4.0 TFSI V8. Where valve deactivation is used, causes lie in the oil supply or in a sticking switching element, and NHTSA's description of GM's lifters with oil-pressure locking pins shows how small leaks spoil the switch. P3473, P3475 and P3476 are the electrical codes of cylinder 10.

causes.label: Oil pressure or oil condition not sufficient to switch cylinder 10
Lifter or cam sleeve at cylinder 10 sticking
Oil screen or passage to the cylinder 10 actuator blocked
Leaking seal at the actuator

symptoms: Tapping noise from the valve train

P3475.title: Cylinder 10 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3475.description: P3475 points to a short to ground on the circuit that controls deactivation or the intake valve of cylinder 10. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. The Lamborghini Huracán's V10 runs on five cylinders at light load and the Aventador V12 on six below 135 km/h, yet neither maker publishes code-level diagnostics, and Audi's sister V10 manages without valve actuators. For a sense of the test, GM's eight-cylinder version of the low check needs below 0.5 ohm to ground while the output is off, sampled every 250 ms. Check the wire to cylinder 10 for chafing first, then the actuator itself. P3473 handles an open line, P3476 a short to voltage, P3479 the exhaust counterpart.

causes.label: Cylinder 10 control wire grounded through chafing
Actuator of cylinder 10 shorted internally
Water in the actuator connector
Defective control module output stage

P3476.title: Cylinder 10 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3476.description: P3476 is logged when the control circuit of the cylinder 10 deactivation or intake valve actuator sits at too high a level, usually a short to a battery-fed wire found while the output is active. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. On the V10s that offer shut-off, Audi describes the bank being stopped by cutting fuel injection and ignition in the upper gears, so cylinder 10 has no valve actuator there. A twelve-cylinder engine with valve switching, such as Mercedes' M137 with its oil-pressure solenoid pack, is the kind of design this code was written for. The control module then usually blocks deactivation for the rest of the trip. Electrical siblings: P3473 and P3475.

causes.label: Cylinder 10 control wire shorted to a supply
Cylinder 10 actuator coil with shorted turns
Control module output stage defective

symptoms: Cylinder deactivation locked out for the drive

P3477.title: Cylinder 10 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3477.description: P3477 belongs to engines that switch the exhaust valve of cylinder 10 through its own actuator, and it reports that this actuator's circuit is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Ten-cylinder engines with shut-off, the Audi R8 V10 and the Lamborghini Huracán, deactivate a bank rather than individual valves; Audi names injection and ignition as what is stopped. GM's patent on valve deactivation shows that the exhaust side has its own timing requirement, with solenoid-driven hydraulic control valves stopping and restarting the exhaust valves ahead of the intake valves. Diagnose as a plain open circuit: connector, wire, coil. P3479 and P3480 are the shorts, P3478 the functional fault, P3473 the intake circuit.

causes.label: Wire to the cylinder 10 exhaust actuator interrupted
Exhaust actuator coil of cylinder 10 open
Corroded actuator connector
Control module output failed

P3478.title: Cylinder 10 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3478.description: P3478 describes a cylinder 10 exhaust valve that does not switch as commanded although its actuator circuit is fine. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. When an exhaust valve keeps working after shut-off, the trapped gas is pumped out and the cylinder cools, which a Ford patent proposes to catch through exhaust pressure. Cooling is also why Bentley alternates the idle bank of its W12 to protect cylinders and converter; Bentley, like Audi on the R8 V10, shuts down banks rather than individual valves. The code therefore only applies to engines with switchable exhaust valves, which none of the known V10 or V12 systems publicly use. P3477, P3479 and P3480 are the electrical faults.

causes.label: Exhaust switching element at cylinder 10 stuck
Oil pressure too low for the exhaust switch
Exhaust actuator responding slowly

symptoms: Harsh jolt as cylinder 10 is reactivated

P3479.title: Cylinder 10 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3479.description: P3479 shows a short to ground, or another cause of a low signal, on the control line of the cylinder 10 exhaust valve actuator. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Engines with ten or more cylinders that deactivate cylinders include Audi's R8 V10, Lamborghini's Huracán V10 and Aventador V12, and Bentley's W12; the published descriptions of all of them talk about whole banks, not about a valve actuator per cylinder. If an engine does carry one, the check mirrors the intake low test known from GM's V8s: resistance to ground with the output off. Repair is wiring or actuator work around cylinder 10. Siblings: P3477 (open), P3480 (high), P3475 (intake low).

causes.label: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 10 shorted to ground
Exhaust actuator shorted internally
Control module output stage faulty

P3480.title: Cylinder 10 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit High
P3480.description: If the control line of the cylinder 10 exhaust valve actuator is held near supply voltage, the engine computer stores P3480. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. A ten-cylinder engine has no cylinder 11 or 12, so P3480 is the last exhaust-valve code a V10 could ever use; the R8 V10 still does without it because its shut-off works through injection and ignition. Sorting out a high circuit means looking for a wire chafed against a feed, a backprobe left in a connector, or a coil with shorted windings. P3477 (open) and P3479 (low) are the other electrical faults of this actuator, P3476 the intake equivalent on cylinder 10.

causes.label: Exhaust actuator wire of cylinder 10 shorted to a feed
Shorted windings in the exhaust actuator coil
Engine control module output defective

P3481.title: Cylinder 11 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3481.description: P3481 marks an open circuit to the actuator for deactivation or the intake valve of cylinder 11, a cylinder only V12 and W12 engines possess. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Bentley's W12, the best documented twelve-cylinder with shut-off, stops one complete bank of six and, according to its engineering chief, leaves the valves operating; the ECU alternates between bank A and bank B using intake and exhaust sensor data so cylinders and catalytic converter stay warm. With no valve actuator, there is no circuit for P3481 to check. On a design that has one, it means a broken wire, connector or coil. P3483 and P3484 report shorts, P3482 the function, P3485 the exhaust side.

causes.label: Wire to the cylinder 11 actuator broken
Cylinder 11 actuator coil open
Actuator connector at cylinder 11 loose or corroded
Driver stage in the engine control module failed

symptoms: Engine stays on all twelve cylinders

P3482.title: Cylinder 11 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Performance
P3482.description: P3482 is the functional check for cylinder 11: the actuator circuit is electrically fine, but the cylinder does not actually go dormant or wake up when told to. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Bentley's Bentayga and Continental W12 can run on six of twelve cylinders, yet the published description has the valves keep working, so a valve-switching failure cannot arise there. Engines that do close valves rely on oil pressure acting on switching lifters, as NHTSA's review of GM's lifter design lays out in detail; contaminated or low oil and worn locking pins are the usual reasons for a missed switch. The electrical counterparts on cylinder 11 are P3481, P3483 and P3484.

causes.label: Contaminated or insufficient oil for switching cylinder 11
Worn or sticking locking pins at cylinder 11
Oil screen to the cylinder 11 actuator clogged
Actuator seal leaking pressure

P3483.title: Cylinder 11 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit Low
P3483.description: P3483 is stored for a low signal on the control circuit of the cylinder 11 deactivation or intake valve actuator, in practice a short to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Cylinder 11 exists only on twelve-cylinder engines; among those with shut-off are Bentley's W12, Lamborghini's Aventador V12 and, historically, Mercedes' M137. GM's analogous V8 test treats under 0.5 ohm to ground with the driver off as a fault once 20 of 25 samples agree, with the enable conditions of 11 V system voltage and 425 rpm. A grounded line can energise the actuator continuously and take cylinder 11 out at the wrong time. Siblings: P3481 (open) and P3484 (high).

causes.label: Cylinder 11 control line shorted to ground
Cylinder 11 actuator shorted internally
Moisture at the actuator connector
Engine control module output faulty

P3484.title: Cylinder 11 Deactivation/Intake Valve Control Circuit High
P3484.description: P3484 signals that the control circuit of the cylinder 11 deactivation or intake valve actuator is too high, for example because its wire is shorted to a battery feed and the module detects it when switching the output on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Twelve-cylinder engines that shut down cylinders, notably the Bentley W12 in Bentayga and Continental GT and the Lamborghini Aventador V12, describe their systems as switching off a whole bank, with Bentley stating that the valves keep moving. P3484 thus fits only a design with a dedicated valve actuator at cylinder 11. The control module will normally cancel deactivation and run on all cylinders. P3481 and P3483 are the remaining electrical faults.

causes.label: Cylinder 11 control wire touching battery voltage
Cylinder 11 actuator coil with shorted turns
Control module driver damaged

P3485.title: Cylinder 11 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit/Open
P3485.description: P3485 is triggered by an open circuit on a separate exhaust valve actuator at cylinder 11. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. Bentley's engineers say their W12 shut-off leaves both valve sets working, and they rotate the dormant bank to keep it hot; Lamborghini's Aventador V12 and Audi's group V10 likewise talk only about banks. No published system on an engine of this size switches the exhaust valve of an individual cylinder. A GM patent explains why exhaust timing is a topic of its own: its hydraulic control valves deactivate the exhaust valves first and bring them back first. Electrically, treat P3485 like any open actuator line. P3487 and P3488 report shorts, P3486 a functional fault.

causes.label: Open wire to the cylinder 11 exhaust actuator
Coil of the cylinder 11 exhaust actuator open
Connector at the exhaust actuator corroded
Engine control module output defective

symptoms: Engine no longer drops to half its cylinders

P3486.title: Cylinder 11 Exhaust Valve Control Performance
P3486.description: P3486 flags a functional problem with the exhaust valve of cylinder 11: the circuit is healthy, but the valve does not reach the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J2012 reserves the codes for cylinders 9 to 12 for engines with more than eight cylinders. With a twelve-cylinder engine the consequences of a valve that keeps opening are that the cylinder pumps cold air through the exhaust and the converter cools, the issue Bentley avoids on its W12 by alternating banks. A Ford patent shows how such a leaking exhaust valve can be spotted from exhaust pressure. The reverse fault, a valve that stays shut, compresses trapped gas when the cylinder returns. As none of the known V12 or W12 systems switches valves individually, there is no documented user. P3485, P3487 and P3488 are the electrical faults.

causes.label: Exhaust switching element of cylinder 11 jammed
Oil supply inadequate for exhaust switching
Exhaust actuator slow to respond

P3487.title: Cylinder 11 Exhaust Valve Control Circuit Low
P3487.description: Cylinder 11 exhaust valve control voltage below expected range — short to ground.
